comparison: Perfect agreement on structure quality and resolution (C4, C35-C43). Both evaluations affirm the high quality of the cryo-EM structure at 3.1 Å resolution with appropriate validation metrics. OpenEval emphasizes technical details while peer reviewers highlight novelty and importance as a milestone.

Complete agreement on methodological innovation (C29-C34, C204). Both evaluations support the novel chimera approach with mVenus and nanobody fusion, and confirm functional validation demonstrates wild-type-like properties. Peer reviewers explicitly praise the novelty of the method.

Strong agreement on gating mechanism and TBZ inhibition (C5-C6, C44, C47-C52, C139, C198-C199). Both evaluations support the structural observations of gate closure and non-competitive inhibition mechanism. Peer reviewers describe insights into 'dead-end' conformation, while OpenEval notes C60 is also relevant but grouped differently by peer reviewers.

Agreement on mutagenesis data for gating residues (C57-C70, C156-C159). Both evaluations support W318's critical role and the differential effects of mutations. Peer reviewers also include conservation claims (C7, C45, C53, C160-C164) in their assessment of the gating mechanism, while OpenEval addresses these separately.

Complete agreement on polar networks (C71-C76, C8, C192-C197). Both evaluations acknowledge the structural identification of polar networks and accept the speculative nature of functional roles in proton transduction. Peer reviewers note the authors appropriately qualify the proposals about coupling to proton translocation.

Strong agreement on TBZ binding site and key interactions (C77-C93). Both evaluations support structural observations and mutagenesis validation of E312, R189, K138, and N34 as critical residues. Peer reviewers also include R189/K138 summary claims (C167-C169) in their assessment, describing binding and transport data as 'convincing.'

Agreement on VMAT2/VMAT1 selectivity determinants (C100-C108, C183). Both evaluations support identification of L37 and V232 as key residues conferring TBZ selectivity. Peer reviewers also include broader selectivity analysis (C170-C182, C184) in their assessment, noting 'well-reasoned conclusions' about selectivity differences.

Agreement on MD simulation results for protonation effects (C117-C121, C185-C191). Both evaluations support the computational predictions about protonation states and their effects. Peer reviewers also include TBZ docking simulations (C109, C111-C116) in their assessment, though they do not comment on MD simulations in detail.

Agreement on MD simulations for DA binding and release (C124-C135). Both evaluations accept the computational findings about water pathway formation and DA release mechanisms. Peer reviewers also include substrate release mechanism claims (C200-C203) in their assessment, acknowledging the speculative elements are appropriately qualified.

Complete agreement on disease mutation analysis (C143-C149). Both evaluations support the structural interpretation of disease mutations, though OpenEval notes functional characterization would strengthen conclusions. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these claims without explicit comment.

Agreement on AlphaFold comparison (C141-C142). Both evaluations support the finding that experimental structure captures features not predicted computationally. Peer reviewer 3 explicitly states 'The comparison with AlphaFold models is enlightening.'

Complete agreement on overall contributions (C205-C207). Both evaluations affirm the significance and impact of the work. Peer reviewers describe it as 'an important milestone' providing 'new opportunities for developing improved therapeutic interventions.'

Agreement on background information and established knowledge (C1-C28). Both evaluations accept the contextual information as properly documented. Peer reviewers also include transport mechanism and gating mechanism discussion claims (C136-C138, C140, C150-C155, C165-C166) in their broader assessment.

OpenEval addresses transport data for binding site mutants (C94-C99) separately, while peer reviewers incorporate this into their broader assessment of TBZ binding site analysis (R6), describing the measurements as enabling 'well-reasoned conclusions.'

OpenEval addresses TBZ docking simulations (C109, C111-C116) separately, while peer reviewers include these computational predictions in their broader assessment of protonation and binding dynamics (R8), noting 'additional biochemical analyses that further support their findings.'

OpenEval addresses gating mechanisms and implications (C150-C155) separately, while peer reviewers incorporate these into their broader assessment of background and mechanistic context (R12), implicitly accepting the interpretations.

OpenEval addresses conservation analysis (C45, C53, C164) separately, while peer reviewers include these claims in their assessment of the gating mechanism (R4), noting implications for the 'wider SLC18 family.'

OpenEval rates E127 and disulfide bond claims (C160-C163, C165-C166) as UNCERTAIN due to speculative interactions, while peer reviewers include some of these claims (C160-C163) in their SUPPORTED assessment of gating residues (R4), without explicitly addressing the uncertainty.
OpenEval addresses R189 and K138 summary (C167-C169) separately, while peer reviewers incorporate these into their broader TBZ binding site assessment (R6), describing the data as 'convincing.'

OpenEval addresses N34 chemical specificity analysis (C170-C181) separately, while peer reviewers include these claims in their broader selectivity assessment (R7), noting 'well-reasoned conclusions about differences in affinity between TBZ derivatives.'

OpenEval addresses VMAT2/VMAT1 selectivity conclusions (C182, C184) separately, while peer reviewers incorporate these into their broader selectivity assessment (R7), supporting the identification of key determinants.

OpenEval addresses substrate release mechanism (C200-C203) separately, while peer reviewers include these claims in their broader assessment of proton coupling and conformational changes (R9), acknowledging the speculative nature is appropriately qualified.
